Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Adult patient presenting with 6-week history of intermittent left ear hearing loss, tinnitus (ringing), and mild intermittent dizziness described as off-balance without vertigo or systemic symptoms  
- No ear pain, discharge, fever, chest pain, or palpitations reported  
- Differential diagnoses consistent with presentation include:  
  • Acoustic neuroma (vestibular schwannoma) – high likelihood given unilateral progressive hearing loss, tinnitus, and dizziness without infection signs  
  • Cerumen impaction – medium likelihood; common and treatable cause; examination prioritized to exclude this first  
  • Meniere’s disease – medium likelihood; tinnitus and intermittent dizziness fit, but lack of classic vertigo episodes and ear fullness noted  
  • Labyrinthitis/vestibular neuritis – low to medium likelihood; presentation less acute and lacks vertigo, pain, or fever  
  • Autoimmune inner ear disease – low likelihood; no systemic symptoms or confirmatory data  
- No contradictions between transcript and DDx; DDx supports clinical reasoning in transcript  
- Examination and possible audiometry needed to narrow diagnosis  

Management Plan
- Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment within 4–5 days for otoscopic ear examination to exclude wax impaction or other ear pathology  
- Provide patient with educational leaflet on tinnitus to improve understanding and awareness  
- Advise patient to contact support team to schedule in-person exam; provide option for video consultation if symptoms worsen or new concerns arise before appointment  
- Plan further investigations (e.g., audiometry, imaging) pending examination findings
